8.day_length_note_seasoned: At the Las Vegas Valley's latitude, about 36 degrees N, grow intermediate-day onions such as Candy or Super Star, which bulb at around 12 to 14 hours of daylight. They are set out in fall or late winter and bulb as days lengthen through spring. A long-day (northern) variety here rarely reaches its longer daylength trigger and bulbs poorly, while a short-day variety may bulb too early and small.

onion.region_notes_seasoned: The Las Vegas Valley grows bulbing onions on a fall-set, spring-bulb cycle, per the UNLV Master Gardener Southern Nevada chart.
